Date: 2026-11-18

Entertainment
• Grand Theft Auto VI launches on Nov. 19 to rave early reviews, with multiple outlets calling it Rockstar’s best yet and noting its ambitious dual-protagonist narrative and expansive simulation. 
• Critics and aggregators peg GTA VI near the top of all-time rankings as hype translates into strong prelaunch buzz and award nods. 
• Amazon founder Jeff Bezos said he was “heavily involved” in the decision to cast Robert Pattinson as the next James Bond, underscoring Big Tech’s growing sway in legacy franchises. 
• Civilization-maker Firaxis cut roughly a third of staff, including its studio head, reflecting ongoing volatility in gaming labor markets despite blockbuster releases elsewhere.
Why it matters: Gaming’s biggest launch in a decade signals continued industry gravity even as studios restructure, while tech’s deepening role in film IP reshapes creative decisions.

Geopolitics & Diplomacy
• Trump, Xi, and Putin are set for a rare three-way meeting in China, with Xi greeting Trump on arrival as all sides seek leverage amid wars, sanctions, and competition. 
• The EU proposed a €45bn loan package to help Ukraine avoid a funding crunch and bolster defenses in 2027. 
• Democrats flipped Alaska’s Senate seat as Mary Peltola’s win capped a strong cycle, potentially reshaping Senate dynamics. 
• Nvidia halted advanced AI chip sales to China, a major strategic shift amid export controls and leadership turmoil. 
• Turkey’s top court imposed a political ban on Istanbul’s opposition mayor Ekrem Imamoglu, tightening Erdoğan’s grip ahead of future contests.
Why it matters: High-level summits and sanctions-era realignments intersect with domestic political shifts and tech decoupling, shaping a more fragmented global order.
Sources: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/ck9d75x5wwwwo https://www.ft.com/content/ae7d1b27-b892-48d6-ad47-41128a4b53a1 https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/18/eu-loan-ukraine-cash-crisis-defences-von-der-leyen-kyiv https://www.npr.org/2026/11/18/g-s1-154145/up-first-newsletter-mary-peltola-alaska-trump-asia-nvidia-tech-issues-ai https://www.theverge.com/tech/1036445/nvidia-h200-ai-chips-china-stop-selling https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-18/turkey-slaps-main-erdogan-rival-imamoglu-with-political-ban

Economy & Markets
• Nvidia beat expectations and raised guidance while assuring continuity post-Huang, buoying AI-driven sentiment even as related shares whipsawed. 
• Anthropic’s IPO is drawing intense retail interest and could price above range, with Amazon and Google poised to own nearly 30% combined post-listing. 
• The ECB warned the AI buildout’s borrowing spree has echoes of the subprime era due to off-balance-sheet commitments by hyperscalers. 
• Nvidia said it will stop selling chips to China and clarified limits on financing “neocloud” data centers, highlighting geopolitical and credit risks. 
• Tesla’s $30,000 Cybercab carries a $299 monthly fee and resale restrictions, spotlighting the shift to subscription-tethered vehicles.
Why it matters: AI’s boom is lifting markets but drawing regulatory scrutiny, balance-sheet risks, and geopolitics into sharp relief as capital floods chips, data centers, and automation.
Sources: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/18/nvidias-numbers-and-anthropic-anticipation-drive-nasdaq-futures-up.html https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/18/anthropic-ipo-retail-investors.html https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/17/amazon-and-google-will-together-own-nearly-30-of-anthropic-after-its-ipo/ https://www.ft.com/content/d16475ce-efce-4dc1-b5a3-2f7c79e9dea9 https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/17/nvidia-is-abandoning-china-after-jensen-huangs-ouster/ https://arstechnica.com/cars/2026/11/tesla-will-sell-you-a-cybercab-for-30000-then-charge-299-a-month-to-use-it/

Armed Conflict & Security
• Kuwait and Bahrain reported Iranian attacks following a U.S. strike on Iran’s Qeshm Island, marking a sharp escalation across Gulf flashpoints. 
• Israel expanded operations into central Gaza and demolished homes in southern Lebanon amid widening fronts. 
• Analysts warned the current U.S.-Iran “status quo” could slip into wider war as tit-for-tat strikes intensify. 
• Ukraine detailed precision strikes that damaged Russia’s Crimea bridge, further isolating occupied territory. 
• U.S. officials said there is “zero” evidence recent tech outages were linked or malicious, even as widespread malware incidents hit major sites.
Why it matters: Cross-theater escalations and cyber uncertainty increase miscalculation risks, threatening regional stability and global trade routes.
Sources: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cw4gn9jeqjq7o https://www.npr.org/2026/11/17/nx-s1-6044255/us-iran-war-latest-bahrain https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/18/palestinians-flee-refugee-camp-as-israel-begins-operation-in-central-gaza https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/18/crimea-is-turning-into-an-island-how-ukraine-hit-putins-prized-bridge https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/18/zero-evidence-recent-tech-outages-linked-marco-rubio https://arstechnica.com/security/2026/11/malicious-code-delivered-through-optimizely-hits-visitors-to-hundreds-of-sites/

Sports
• Cameron Bancroft claimed Australia’s entire team knew about the 2018 sandpaper tampering, intensifying scrutiny on current captain Pat Cummins. 
• England won the ODI series in Australia with a dominant third match, powered by a Duckett century and disciplined bowling. 
• The Premier League’s incidents panel found six on-field referee errors in the last round, a joint-record, reigniting officiating debates. 
• Ivan Toney’s assault trial will overlap Euro 2028 after an unsuccessful bid to avoid a scheduling clash.
Why it matters: Integrity controversies and officiating standards continue to shape fan trust, while elite performances reset competitive narratives ahead of major tournaments.
Sources: https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/articles/cmqlqdevgl9ro https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/articles/c6vg28end00xo https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c69q8jy924y4o https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/ckm2m1899mqyo

Society & Human Rights
• Mada Masr editor Lina Attalah faces retrial in Egypt, highlighting ongoing press freedom pressures. 
• An Iraqi conservationist who was kidnapped by militias continues efforts to save the country’s marshes, underscoring environmental human rights risks. 
• Spain’s National Court reopened an investigation into Julio Iglesias over sexual abuse allegations by two former employees. 
• Internal documents suggest Meta’s school “safety” program also aimed to boost teen user growth on Instagram, raising platform responsibility questions. 
• UK political debate flared over welfare and disability comments, prompting calls to retract “crass” remarks defending cuts.
Why it matters: Press freedoms, workplace abuse claims, platform accountability, and social policy rhetoric directly affect vulnerable communities and democratic norms.
Sources: https://www.aljazeera.com/video/newsfeed/2026/11/18/aje-onl-nf_lina-attalah-of-mada-masr-on-trial-181126 https://www.npr.org/2026/11/18/nx-s1-6043167/iraq-environmentalist-marshes-iran-backed-militia-kidnapped https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/18/spanish-court-investigates-julio-iglesias-two-women-allegations https://www.theverge.com/tech/1036517/instagram-school-safety-program-project-gryffindor https://www.theguardian.com/politics/live/2026/nov/18/shabana-mahmood-andy-burnham-kemi-badenoch-pmqs-latest-news-updates

Art & Culture
• Berlin’s Kollwitzplatz celebrates the legacy of Käthe Kollwitz, whose work on war and childhood resonates with today’s visitors. 
• India’s “How Love Moves” won an IDFA co-production award, while DOC NYC’s “Dryads” explored musical creation across cultures. 
• Boston’s MFA announced “Taylor Swift: The Eras Collection,” featuring 50+ artifacts charting the star’s career. 
• Stone Island brought its NO SEASONS installation to Shanghai Art Week, blending fashion, materials, and art.
Why it matters: Cultural institutions and festivals are amplifying diverse narratives that bridge contemporary audiences, heritage, and global creative exchange.
Sources: https://www.npr.org/2026/11/18/nx-s1-6043021/berlin-kollwitzplatz-statue https://variety.com/2026/film/global/india-how-love-moves-idfa-industry-section-awards-1236951872/ https://www.billboard.com/music/pop/taylor-swift-eras-collection-boston-museum-fine-arts-details-1236384740/ https://hypebeast.com/2026/11/stone-island-brings-no-seasons-to-shanghai-art-week-2026

Climate & Environment
• China’s provincial coal cuts contrast with U.S. lagging climate tech deployment, widening divergence between the two biggest emitters. 
• A methane-laced landfill incident in Los Angeles County triggered emergency orders for resident care, highlighting waste and air quality risks. 
• Hydropower in the U.S. Southwest fell 28% vs. the 10-year average due to drought, straining clean power portfolios. 
• Commentary urged AI data centers to avoid fossil power as communities push back on their energy footprint. 
• Offshore wind farms are creating artificial reefs, drawing fish and scrutiny from fishers amid ecosystem changes.
Why it matters: Climate mitigation is colliding with infrastructure, drought, and industrial growth, demanding faster clean energy transitions and better local safeguards.
Sources: https://www.npr.org/2026/11/18/nx-s1-6044646/china-and-the-u-s-emissions-cop31-antalya https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/18/los-angeles-landfill-explosion-housing https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/11/17/1148742/hydropower-drought-colorado-river/ https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-026-03708-6 https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/18/offshore-wind-farms-artificial-reef-experiment-fishing-industry https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/18/uk-government-angela-eagle-natural-england-wild-birds-decline-

Health & Pandemic
• A three-year-old died following a medical emergency at a Greater Manchester nursery; police are investigating. 
• Leading voices predict gut microbiome profiles will become part of routine medical records over coming decades. 
• New research shows plasma p-tau217 and p-tau217/Aβ42 perform comparably to CSF biomarkers for detecting Alzheimer’s pathology.
Why it matters: Advances in diagnostics and personalized health are accelerating, even as communities confront acute care tragedies requiring robust safety and oversight.
Sources: https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026/nov/18/boy-three-dies-medical-emergency-cosy-toes-nursery-middleton-greater-manchester https://www.newscientist.com/article/2597569-the-gut-microbiome-will-become-part-of-every-persons-medical-record/ https://www.nature.com/articles/s43587-026-01259-z

Artificial Intelligence
• OpenAI unveiled GPT‑6.2 Astra and Sol, touting improved professional outputs and efficiency across ChatGPT Work, Codex, and APIs. 
• Google rebranded its Spark agent as “Tasks” and made it free, while Microsoft embedded Office apps inside Copilot, positioning it as a new “OS for work.” 
• Osmo claimed its AI can detect and describe odors on par with human noses, built on a vast chemo-sensory dataset. 
• AI-linked hurried patching may have contributed to U.S. tech outages, as organizations rushed to fix AI-identified bugs. 
• Disney and AWS introduced AI-powered “Star Wars” robots that react in real time to guests and each other.
Why it matters: AI is rapidly permeating productivity, science, and entertainment, raising reliability, governance, and safety questions as deployments scale.
Sources: https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-6-2-astra-sol https://www.theverge.com/tech/1035756/google-spark-ai-tasks-free https://arstechnica.com/gadgets/2026/11/microsoft-calls-copilot-the-new-os-for-work-at-ignite-keynote/ https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/11/18/1148816/smell-startup-osmo-ai-nose-good-as-humans/ https://www.ft.com/content/96c565f1-f229-40b6-91e8-7a849ec4b208 https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/digital/new-star-wars-robots-disney-amazon-ai-anzellans-1236757851/

Longevity & Anti-Aging
• Researchers outlined synaptic dysfunction as a key driver of cognitive decline and discussed therapeutic strategies targeting synapses. 
• Senescent mesenchymal stromal cells may impair stem cell activity, positioning them as significant contributors to degenerative aging. 
• A senolytic vaccine showed promise by clearing senescent cells and improving dendritic cell function in preclinical work. 
• Clinicians highlighted protecting and reinvigorating the senses as a strategy to reduce dementia risk.
Why it matters: Targeting cellular senescence and synaptic health, alongside sensory maintenance, could reshape prevention and treatment of age-related decline.
Sources: https://www.fightaging.org/archives/2026/11/age-related-synaptic-dysfunction-and-possible-approaches-to-treatment/ https://www.fightaging.org/archives/2026/11/senescence-in-mesenchymal-stromal-cells-as-a-driver-of-degenerative-aging/ https://www.fightaging.org/archives/2026/11/a-senolytic-vaccine-that-also-improves-dendritic-cell-function/ https://peterattiamd.com/guarding-and-reinvigorating-the-senses-to-protect-against-dementia/

Science & Technology
• NASA’s Voyager 1 reached one light-day from Earth after 49 years, a landmark in interstellar exploration. 
• ULA’s Vulcan Centaur failed during a launch carrying 40 Amazon satellites due to a first-stage issue identified minutes after liftoff. 
• San Diego will shut down 500+ Flock cameras and smart streetlights, reversing a major surveillance tech deployment. 
• Rivian spinoff Also paused e‑bike deliveries over battery and software bugs, underscoring hardware–software integration challenges. 
• Danish researchers unveiled an optimal algorithmic approach to the 174-year-old four-color map problem.
Why it matters: Space milestones, infrastructure failures, public tech rollbacks, and mathematical advances all shape the trajectory of technology’s impact on society and industry.
Sources: https://www.space.com/space-exploration/voyager/1-light-day-from-earth-nasas-voyager-1-probe-hits-huge-milestone-in-interstellar-space https://www.theverge.com/science/1036431/nasa-voyager-1-light-day-milestone https://www.space.com/space-exploration/launches-spacecraft/ula-lost-a-vulcan-centaur-rocket-carrying-40-amazon-satellites-10-minutes-after-launch-but-the-failure-began-just-after-liftoff https://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2026/11/san-diego-dumps-both-flock-cameras-and-smart-streetlights/ https://www.theverge.com/transportation/1036460/also-rivian-spinoff-tm-b-ebike-delivery-delay-software-battery-issues https://phys.org/news/2026-11-danish-efficient-solution-famous-year.html

Other
• Nature shared short video primers to improve conference networking, emphasizing preparation and practice. 
• An editorial on “the right to do wrong” weighed ethical and philosophical dimensions of equal chance and liberty.
Why it matters: Professional skills and ethical reflection underpin effective research cultures and public discourse.

Entertainment.title: 'Avengers: Doomsday' Runtime Reportedly Confirmed
Entertainment.text: SummaryA new report suggests the standard version of the upcoming film will clock in at just under two and a half hoursMarvel Studios President Kevin Feige recently confirmed Robert Downey Jr is playing Victor Von Doom rather than an Iron Man variantRecent developments also tease the return of Scarlet Witch and the involvement of Deadpool and WolverineThis post may contain spoilers. Entertainment.title: Ford Celebrates Henry Ford’s First Race Win With the Mustang GTD 1901
Entertainment.text: SummaryHonors Henry Ford’s 1901 "Sweepstakes" race car with a Royal Red exterior, black stripes, and exposed carbon fiber.Featuring Mahogany Red leather, suede, and F-22 fighter jet titanium hardware.Orders open December 2026 for Q2 2027 delivery.Ford has officially unveiled the 2028 Ford Mustang GTD 1901, an exclusive special edition that pays homage to the roots of the brand. Celebrating Henry Ford’s legendary 1901 victory in the two-cylinder “Sweepstakes” race car, the win that secured the financial backing to start the Ford Motor Company, the GTD 1901 merges racing heritage with cutting-edge engineering. Visually, the GTD 1901 turns the vintage black and deep red palette of the original Sweepstakes into a striking modern livery. The car is draped in a deep Royal Red finish, contrasted by an off-center black racing stripe split by a bright red centerline. Diagonal lines running off the strip inject a sense of motion, while exposed carbon fiber covers much of the car’s aero, including its towering active rear wing. To ensure the GTD 1901 lives up to its name, Ford’s aerodynamic performance Package comes standard, and buyers can opt for magnesium wheels in Black or Luster Nickel to shave over 50 pounds of unsprung weight.In contrast to the usual spartan interiors of track weapons, the GTD 1901’s interior is decorated with luxurious and bespoke touches. The seats are wrapped in Mahogany Red leather detailed with contrasting Race Red stitching, a hue extends to the seatbelt edges to echo the exterior stripe. Full-grain leather covers the instrument panel, door panels, and center console, while Mahogany Red suede lines the inner portion of the steering wheel. To give the car an extra special touch, Ford used 3D-printed titanium reclaimed from retired F-22 Raptor fighter jets for the lengthened paddle shifters, shock-tower-inspired gear selector, and a serialized passenger dashboard VIN plaque.Underneath the skin lies Ford’s iconic 5.2-liter supercharged V8 cranking out 815 horsepower and 664 lb-ft of torque to the rear wheels via an eight-speed dual-clutch transmission. Orders for the 2028 Ford Mustang GTD 1901 are slated to open in late 2026, with deliveries expected to begin in Q2 2027, joining the Liquid Carbon editions in offering collectors a bespoke take on American supercar engineering.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Brad Pitt Reveals 'Ocean's 14' Filming Delayed Until Late 2027
Entertainment.text: SummaryBrad Pitt has confirmed that the highly anticipated fifth installment of the Ocean's franchise will not begin filming until late 2027   Informat.roThe heist movie will feature the return of original cast members George Clooney, Julia Roberts, Matt Damon, and Don Cheadle, with David Leitch directing   NewsBytesPitt also discussed his upcoming role in 'The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth', a sequel penned by Quentin Tarantino and directed by David FincherBrad Pitt has officially provided an update on the production schedule for the highly anticipated Ocean’s 14. Speaking at the Hollywood premiere of his latest film, the actor confirmed that the next chapter in the iconic heist franchise will not begin shooting until late 2027, shifting from its previously scheduled start date next month.Despite the delay, the fifth installment of the beloved Ocean's series is gearing up to be a massive reunion. Pitt confirmed that George Clooney, Julia Roberts, Matt Damon, and Don Cheadle are all set to reprise their legendary roles, with David Leitch tapped to direct the project. Set a few years after the original film in 1970s Los Angeles, the project sees Cliff transitioning from Hollywood stunt work to a movie theater projectionist and occasional hitman. While Tarantino penned the script, directing duties were handed over to David Fincher, marking a reunion between Fincher and Pitt 32 years after their collaboration on Seven. Entertainment.title: Cardón Tavern Turns DUMBO House Into a Tableside Steakhouse
Entertainment.text: SummarySoho House has opened Cardón Tavern, its new contemporary steakhouse concept, at DUMBO House in BrooklynThe menu leans on steakhouse and tavern classics, with steak tartare and a wagyu tomahawk both served tablesideCocktails like the Dirty Agave Martini and mezcal-based San Luis Swizzle point to a sister restaurant arriving at Soho Beach House Los Cabos in early 2027Soho House has opened Cardón Tavern at DUMBO House, introducing its new contemporary steakhouse concept to Brooklyn. Named after a cactus native to Baja California, the restaurant pairs big steakhouse portions and a deep drinks list with the easygoing feel of a neighborhood tavern.The starters stick to New York steakhouse staples, with a few made at the table. A New England Crab Cake and Shrimp Cocktail with horseradish sit next to East and West Coast oysters. The Steak Tartare is finished tableside, which makes even the first course feel like a bit of a show.The mains are built around hand-picked steaks, led by a wagyu tomahawk brought out and presented at the table. For non-beef eaters, there’s whole fish, lobster and a chicken stuffed with truffle. Dessert brings the house Cardón Sundae and a Chocolate Soufflé served with warm chocolate sauce and vanilla ice cream, along with Apple Crumble and New York Cheesecake.The bar program is where Cardón’s Los Cabos connection shows most. The Dirty Agave Martini mixes Patrón Reposado with tomolive brine, the San Luis Swizzle is built on mezcal, and a Cobbler uses Patrón Añejo. A classic Manhattan, a Cosmopolitan and a dedicated martini menu cover the New York side, backed by a sommelier-chosen wine list and a short selection of draft beers.DUMBO House’s dining room has been redesigned around the new concept. Long tables are set up for group dinners, with exposed wood and warm brass under dim lighting to keep the room intimate. Running the kitchen is Head of Culinary Jonathan Benno, formerly of Per Se and Lincoln Ristorante, with VP of Culinary Joshua Brown, who previously worked at Groot Hospitality and Wolfgang Puck. Director of Bar and Beverage Mark Murphy, who comes from STARR Restaurants, and New York Area Head of Bars and Beverage Javier Salgado, formerly of Schroeder Hospitality Group, lead the drinks.Cardón Tavern serves dinner at DUMBO House Tuesday through Saturday, with reservations available through the Soho House app.DISCLAIMER: We discourage irresponsible and/or underage drinking. Art & Culture.title: Vibram Opens the Doors to Its North Brookfield Factory for Second Annual Creator Program
Art & Culture.text: Most people recognize Vibram by the signature yellow octagon on the bottom of their favorite boots, though far fewer have seen where those outsoles actually come from. From November 4 to 6, the brand opened the doors of its US headquarters in North Brookfield, Massachusetts, for the second edition of Made in North Brookfield. This year’s program brought together 15 creators, designers and brand partners from across the US and Canada, including Nicole McLaughlin, Ella Emhoff, Bailey Goldberg, John Chen of ArchivePDF, Gabriele Fazi of Kith and Victoria Wells of Arc’teryx. The three days centered on New England craft and American bootmaking heritage.North Brookfield is Vibram’s primary US manufacturing center, with factory roots in Massachusetts dating back to 1965. Now owned by Vibram, the plant makes soles for everything from industrial footwear to a classic American boot. It is one of the only rubber outsole factories operating in the US.The experience kicked off with a tour led by Christopher Nikopoulos, Vibram’s US VP of Operations, following the process from start to finish. In compounding, raw rubber is blended with custom performance formulas and colors. Milling then rolls the rubber into precise sheets, known as “breads,” ready for molding. Finally, in the molding presses, heat and high pressure vulcanize the sheets into finished outsoles with their final shape and tread.From there, the creators took over. In the boot and sole workshop, each one chose a custom rubber colorway and tread. They worked with either rubber pellets or shapes cut from rubber sheets, and placed the rubber into the molds themselves. The signature moment came with the yellow octagon: a separate piece of yellow rubber, made from its own special compound, set into the mold as the brand’s mark of quality.With the soles complete, focus shifted to the uppers. Supported by Easymoc, one of Maine’s last traditional bootmakers, the workshop used handcrafted Old Port uppers from the brand’s Lewiston workshop. Master cobblers Michele Pirrone and Refugio Contreras guided creators step by step through lasting, cementing the soles to the uppers and hand-stitching the finished pairs.At midday, bench work paused for “cucinare insieme,” or cooking together, with Matteo Ceppi, owner of Sugo Milano. The session brought a taste of Vibram’s Italian heritage into the factory and put guests and technical staff around the same table. It reflects the hospitality the brand extends to both visitors and its own employees. Italian touches ran through the program, down to panettoni from Peck.Mornings started outdoors. Guests took a hike through New England woods, testing Vibram footwear in its natural element, and joined a FiveFingers session focused on natural foot movement and the brand’s innovation roots. On November 6, the group returned to North Brookfield to finish their footwear. They then headed to Vibram’s Boston Innovation Lab for a closing party that drew local creatives, industry peers and workshop guests, and ended with the team making spaghetti together. Every creator left with their own one-of-one pair.“This moment is our way of expressing deep appreciation and attachment to American manufacturing and culture, all brought together with a touch of authentic Italian heritage,” said Vibram. For Victoria Wells, the experience left a lasting impression. “I left with a whole lot of new knowledge, a deeper appreciation for the craftsmanship, care, and process that go into making each sole, and an even bigger appreciation for the generosity and hospitality of the Vibram team,” she said.Explore more of Vibram’s production at vibram.com.Read more at Hypebeast

Art & Culture.title: Stone Island Brings NO SEASONS to Shanghai Art Week 2026
Art & Culture.text: Stone Island took NO SEASONS to Shanghai Art Week 2026, staging a dedicated installation at Capsule Plaza Shanghai @ IYOUTH from November 10 to 15. Designed with Milan studio NM3, the space marked the installation's China debut following its first outing at Milan Design Week in April.First launched by Massimo Osti between 1989 and 1994, NO SEASONS returns as a study in a single silhouette. One hooded jacket comes in six proprietary fabrics: Tela Resinata, Nylon Prismatico-TC, Raso Gommato, David-TC, Crinkle Reps NY and Panno. All six are dyed in lead-gray "piombo," so the material does the talking. Standouts include Tela Resinata, an evolution of the brand's foundational Tela Stella canvas, and David-TC, garment-dyed under pressure at up to 130°C for a compressed, textured hand.NM3 carried that logic into the space. Four powder-coated steel benches, upholstered in the same six fabrics, anchored the room, while the jackets sat on black metal shelving raised to eye level on a new plinth. "NO SEASONS is all about material. And so is our work," NM3 co-founder Nicolò Ornaghi told Hypebeast. "We solve all the design problem[s] basically using one single detail. So it's a metal sheet that is bent and screwed. That's it."Co-founder Francesco Zorzi saw the same approach in the collection. "It's actually the same attitude that Stone Island operated with in this collection," he said. "It's one jacket, one design, extremely well done, crazy good details, that works all season."An LED wall screened the collection's new global campaign film by Capsule, while SYLOW, the new Stone Island Sound system, powered a week of live sets from BYYB.Radio. The program also included a talk between NM3 and architect Guo Liaohui of Atelier Guo, and a collectors' panel moderated by Hypebeast China Editor-in-Chief Phil Gong.Asked to sum up the project in one word, Zorzi chose "rigorous." Ornaghi went with "very autonomous." "It's a very statement project from Stone Island I guess," he said. "And we tried to follow this and to have a very recognizable design and installation that can travel and be adapted to different spaces."Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Artificial Intelligence.title: IEEE Celebrates 10 Years of Incorporating Ethics Into AI Systems
Artificial Intelligence.text: Policymakers, technologists, and members of the public have raised concerns about the harm AI’s rapid advancement might cause to society. Their concerns include bias, data privacy violations, the spread of misinformation, and losing control of AI agents.Those issues are relatively new to many people, but the IEEE Standards Association has been working for the past decade on ways to prioritize the responsible development of AI systems.In 2016 IEEE SA launched the IEEE Global Initiative for Ethical Considerations in Autonomous and Intelligent Systems (A/IS) and published the Ethically Aligned Design report. EAD’s mission is to encourage everyone involved in designing autonomous and intelligent systems to prioritize human well-being by applying ethical considerations for the benefit of humanity.Developed by a multidisciplinary community of experts from around the world, the report outlined eight foundational principles for A/IS. They include human rights, people’s well-being, and transparency. More than 100 leading AI ethics experts provided input. EAD’s Version II report was released in 2017. Both versions solicited public input and received hundreds of pages of feedback, according to John C. Havens, who was the global initiative’s founding executive director, and is now the global director for IEEE Planet Positive 2030. And by 2019, there were more than 400 contributors and the community continues to grow.“Ethically Aligned Design was the first of its kind in the sense of a report that was more than a list of principles and from an organization with the credibility of IEEE,” Havens says. “At the time it was released, there wasn’t anything like it.”Since its launch, a series of standards has been developed to provide practical guidelines on designing, building, and deploying technology that prioritizes human values. Several AI ethics certification programs have been introduced.This year marks the 10th anniversary of EAD’s first draft. To celebrate, IEEE SA recently launched a website, a podcast series, and a blog that reflect on the report’s achievements and impact.Eight guiding principlesThe word ethics is often used interchangeably with morality, but that is not the case in responsible AI systems design, according to EAD’s first version. The report includes insights from classical ethics traditions and value-based design methodologies to offer actionable recommendations for engineers developing AI tools.The report established eight foundational general principles for designing autonomous and intelligent systems: respecting human rights, prioritizing increased well-being as success criteria for development, empowering individuals with data agency to have control over their identity, effectiveness, transparency, accountability, awareness of misuse, and competence for the system creators.The principles shift applied ethics to the design stage of AI systems, compared with being a concern after they’re released, the authors wrote. A suite of standards The IEEE 7000 series of standards has been developed based on EAD’s framework. Currently the series consists of 29 projects, 11 of which have been published, and more are still being added. They cover topics such as ethical system design model process (IEEE 7000-2021), AI system transparency (IEEE 7001-2021), data privacy (IEEE 7002-2022), algorithmic bias considerations (IEEE 7003-2024), the impact on people’s well-being (IEEE 7010-2020), machine-readable personal privacy requirements (IEEE 7012-2025), and systems that mimic human empathy (IEEE 7014-2024).AI ethics certificationsIEEE SA offers a suite of ethics in AI programs including IEEE CertifAIEd, which includes two certifications: one for individuals and one for products.The professional certification provides individuals with skills to assess autonomous and intelligent systems for adherence to IEEE’s methodology and ethics criteria.“Ethically Aligned Design was the first of its kind in the sense of a report that was more than a list of principles and from an organization with the credibility of IEEE.” —John C. Havens, founding executive director of the global initiativeThe product certification program assesses whether an organization’s AI tool or system conforms to the criteria in the IEEE Ontological Specifications. A CertifiAIEd assessor evaluates the product to ensure it meets the criteria. Upon completion of the assessment, the owner submits it to the IEEE Conformity Assessment Program, which can certify it and issue the certification mark.IEEE SA also recently released its Responsible AI for Children certification program. This program certifies that AI products for children have been independently tested and verified to meet design and ethics requirements.New industry connections groupThe IEEE Artificial Intelligence Systems (AIS) for Global Flourishing Collaborative Industry Collections group was formed to provide the resources, knowledge, and tools needed to prioritize people’s well-being to developers of AI systems. It has more than 200 members.The collaborative describes its work as a practical, systems-level framework for responsible technology design that translates flourishing into applied methods, metrics, and tools that can be used throughout the AIS lifecycle.The group is establishing guidelines for how to design, evaluate, and govern systems that can measurably improve human well-being and ecological sustainability.Subcommittees are focused on cognition, education, faith, planetary care, spirituality, and other issues.“The group is building directly off the well-being chapter of Ethically Aligned Design and the IEEE 7010 standard (Recommended Practice for Assessing the Impact of Autonomous and Intelligent Systems on Human Well-Being),” Havens says. “That’s on purpose because if human and planetary flourishing aren’t addressed first in design, then human well-being and planetary sustainability are afterthoughts.”Podcasts and blogs To mark the 10-year anniversary, IEEE SA created the five-part “Ethically Aligned Design: 10 Years of Impact” podcast series. It launched on 21 October. New episodes are being released every two weeks.The episodes center around the vision for EAD, the process for selecting its foundational principles, and how they were translated into the IEEE 7000 standards. The first podcast, “Origins of Ethically Aligned Design,” explored early efforts to make ethics a practical part of AI and autonomous system design. The experts discussed challenges, debates, global collaboration, and the real-world impact that helped move responsible technology from ethical principles toward actionable standards and practices.The second podcast, “The Chapters and Committees” focuses on the multidisciplinary groups that worked on turning broad human values into practical guidance for AI and autonomous systems.The podcast discussions serve as material for a thought leadership program that also includes blog articles about the IEEE 7000 series and educational resources to continue to raise awareness and support of this groundbreaking work.This article was updated on 18 November 2026.
